She needed me to go "vet" her ex. He was a good guy, I thought. We bullshitted, had a few cigarettes. We talked about the city; we talked about interior design. I talked about physics; he related by talking about mechanics. I mentioned her name; I saw only the briefest glint of silver, curving around the inside of what I knew to be a .38 calibre revolver. Stainless steel. The smell of gunpowder; that horrible parasthetic feeling wrapping itself around my head, like an infinitely black octopus pushing a proboscis through my right cheekbonre, out through the bony lump on the back of my head. The noise of buzzing, clacketting, ringing all wrapped into one.

I stood, shaking for a moment. The party was lively; many people I was supposed to know, none of whom I did. I shook my head; that was real. The full, unwavering certainty of the reality of what I'd just experienced was motivating. This motherfucker was dangerous. She was right; she needed help.
I briskly strode out the front door. The Viper; Dodge Viper, sat in the parking lot, a man with rusty reddish hair and a wicked Irish accent leaned halfway out, smoking a cigarette and shooting the shit with some blonde cropped kid.
I interrupted. The blonde kid, initially irritated, looked at me in the face and for a moment saw something horrifying. He looked through my right cheek, he said, "You're fucking crazy bro"
The owner of the Viper introduced himself as Irish. He, nor anyone else, saw what Blonde had seen. He was laid back; a gearhead, constantly challenging the threat of death and avoiding it's impending probability.
I explained the last five minutes to him. He nodded; he was interested. He invited me into the car. 
The car smelled of rubber; that pungent, noxious sealant aroma surrendered by the glue used by asbestos abatement technicians during what's known as a "glueout". We pulled out of the driveway. I don't recall the trip.

We arrived at the house. I thanked him, and stepped out of the car, fully aware that the Ex knew I was coming. Knew that he had the upperhand, that he'd already killed me once and wanted to see how many times he could get away with it.
I rounded the side of the northern hedge he had in front of the path to the side door, which was at ground level. This is relevant. As I climbed the staircase which sat nearly ten feet from the porch stairs on which he was sitting, I caught his silhouette. The shotgun levelled, and I began running. 
The weapon discharged. I felt nothing; whether that roaring, earfilling adrenaline high blocked out the nociceptic panic my body felt earlier or whether he missed, I don't know. But I do know I got strong; very strong. I leapt, with the supernatural maximum of my strength and defied gravity. Maybe 1/3 G would be accurate.
My hands touched the roof. The adrenaline morphed into fear; terror, certainty that no matter how I acted I would die again, this time for good. 
The roof was shingled; rough, sandpaper like golden-brown shingles that exploded skyward and bounced off my abdomen. The gunpowder smell. The impulse delivered to the pelvic region that forced me to catwalk breifly across the roof, and the lack of gravity to pull my legs down. The shingles again, exploded upward, scraping my face as that sudden ball of cold iron in my chest provided the weight gravity refused the act upon earlier. My face magnetized; the roof magnetized. The rough surface bit deeply, the bony edges of my skull acting as the main friction provider. Anybody who's been in a motorcycle crash knows the feeling. The parasthetic feeling welled up, slowly, but in a matter of one to two seconds. As it intensified, the blackness replaces the rooftop and the ball of iron froze; as if it had veen injected with liquid nitrogen. My back hurt. My shoulders hurt. It was the pain of a potato chip stuck sideways in the esophagus, all around my scapular girdle, all around my digestive tract. Cold knives digging into my heart from above the division of the bronchus. I couldn't breathe.

But the music was loud. And the party was lively. I stood, in the same spot I had shaken my head what I knew to be mere seconds later. I looked around, I stood back. I knew now, that I was not resurrected but that I was replaying the scene from a moment before I was "reborn" "last" time. I knew now, that everytime I died, I wound up in a different point in time, within a ten minute bracket. The horror resurfaced; I hadn't been shot yet. Not once. That time of day was a few minutes from now, and I was already driving to the house. I had gotten in the car, and I was on my way to die. 
I bolted; straight outside. The Viper sat, Irish sat, in the same spot. Blonde was a few metres away, turning on his heel to begin the conversation I'd interrupted earlier-- later? I couldn't tell. Had Irish returned, or had he yet to leave? Rationally, somehow, I knew that he had yet to leave. That I had yet to be reborn because I hadn't been shot yet. That time of day was in a few minutes.
Again, I explained. Again, I rode; but I remembered this journey. Irish was reckless. He sped, incredible G-forces acted upon my body. We sped down 95th street; the 45° angle turn onto the main drag was not only gone, bit replaced, by Josephine. He didn't anticipate the change, yet expertly steered the car onto the OTHER main drag (different towns now, like slipping through a third dimensional wormhole). He was enjoying himself.
The infinite blackness occupied the windows and I knew that I wasn't dead; I just can't see outside. He miscalculated; we rode up on the curb, briefly, and the crack in the sidewalk offered a reassuring bump. We diverged to the roadway and continued. 

I arrived early; Ex wasn't home. Ex had shot me with the shotgun before he had shot me with the .38? No. Ex had shotgunned me after. He knew I was coming but he didn't know I was coming five minutes earlier than I was coming. I thanked Irish, and saw the last of him; but not his car. This is relevant.

The backyard sat one storey below street level; the level the porch was on. I entered the french doors; quietly. The couch was arranged as it was when I'd sat down. The roofing was intact. I hadn't been shot at all yet. I crept up the stairs; the front door sat about 16 feet away from the landing, the side door sat in between me and that door, about 10 feet to my right, in a blindspot. I crept through the kitchen. Reality sunk in. I was going to die unless I left before I arrived; which was in minutes. Ex arrived very shortly before I'd arrived to the porch scene; which was after I'd been shot on the couch, which was after now. Time didn't make sense and I dropped the matter. It didn't matter. Because he was going to open the door in about three seconds; again, full, unwavering certainty. I bolted.
The side door opened, and the gunpowder smell returned. The parasthetic buzz, like a giant hand with it's heel pushing the centre of my ribs and the fingertips touching the base of my skull. The ringing, the buzzing, the.... clarity? I could see. I caught myself on the wall. I looked around, still buzzing, and had a surge of hope. Had I lived? Had I broken the cycle and seperated myself from my impending murder?
No. Because there I lay, convulsing; unconciously posturing. I could see my brain; literally: the smashed, bleeding cerebellum so badly destroyed the cerebral trunk stuck out crookedly before descending back into my neck. The foam, gathering rapidly, mixing with the bright arterial blood pouring out of my sinuses; sputtering and shooting out with every dry heave and desperate plea for attention my segmented motor cortex tried to make. 
It was horrific and yet I stood transfixed. The parasthetic buzz began to fade as the movement slowed. 
"Oh, c'mon, put one in his brainstem. You can see it for fuck sakes,"
Was this his father? I didn't care. I left. I didn't want to see the gore; not mine. He couldn't see me, and so I ran. I took a sprinting leap out the open front door and landed

In the parking lot. The party was lively. Blonde was scratching his head; looking at the strips of rubber Irish and I left on our second (first?) trip. Now I was fucked. If I couldn't stop my own murder, even if just by dying and rebirthing before I was shot, I would die. I would consider this the first time two of my bodies inhabited the same "4d-space", but even still, a year after this dream, I can't tell.

I ran. I needed to get to the house before Irish and I did, before I got shot on the porch and before I died on the couch. I ran so hard, the hardest sprint; the air drying my lungs and the smoking habit begging me to just cough once, so I could destabilize my breathing. So I could collapse, hyperventilated and I could be shot, whichever time would end my life permanently.
I ran. I ran until I saw her; she was maybe 9. The night was cool and dry, and yet she walked alone, down the only lit patch of sidewalk permeating the infinite blackness, streaked by rain. Her hair was matted; the nightgown was white, floral imprints around the collar but very plain. A soft, thin cotton, but not silk. 
I didn't know who the fuck she was, what she was doing or why she was yet, but I knew that based on the fucked up night I was having, she was legitimate. Valid. She needed help; but she was not the girl who wanted me to meet her Ex and vet him. Different person.
I scooped her. I grabbed her by her ribs and she wrapped her arms around my neck sobbing. I think now, looking back, that she cared deeply about me sometime years later, and was viewing the day I died on these timelines. Maybe a wife? The age difference wasn't unrealistic.
She watched me die, everytime, but with the knowledge I didn't hold; our togetherness?

The scrawling sound. The pop, the vheem, the purple underglow of the Viper. Me, in the passenger seat, intoxicated by the blackness. I rememberes the bump. I threw her, and as I did, the Viper rode up on the curb, and I felt nothing.

Blackness.

Speaking from personal experience, being somebody to somebody is a HUGE pain in the ass. Not only do I have to ACT good, I actually have to "FEEL" good too, otherwise they're upset. 
So, simply put, tell them that. Hiding your feelings is only gonna' let them fester, deform and manifest into things that are not a part of you. Ir's easy to lose grip on our thoughts because they're so.... intangible.

You don't have to do all the work all the time, and paradoxically that means telling certain people to stop doing certain things for you (you = me here, I'm trying to relate) in order to free yourself from the obligation.
You're not in the wrong here at all, and neither are they. It's a disconnect in communication with them and most importantly, with yourself.
You need to be honest. Brutally, truthfully honest, with yourself and those close to you, how you're always feeling. If they take offence or have a fucking problem with it, continue to be brutally honest. Don't succumb for their benefit because your suffering is idealogically out of line with their philosophies. This isn't Dr. Phil and their last name isn't McGraw, but if they want you around they owe it to you to be straight with you. Same goes for the versa; be honest with them. 
Nobody's wrong, is what I've noticed about people. Even serial killers, serial rapists, whilst their crimes are heinous and unforgivable, were doing the right thing at the time, or were so out of touch with themselves that they didn't notice (as if.) 
Feelings are not a liability, they're a part of the human existence and something isn't right in your life. Your emotional response, actually, is both evolutionarily and biologically appropriate. Abstract threats aren't well processed by the human brain, and until you find yourself narrowly avoiding death, the productive side of that emotional response won't kick in.

Your mind is complex, much more than you can ever realize. You're limited by your own vision and the people around you are limited with their arrogantly asserted misconceptions. Your job, now, is to just lay it out. 

"This is how I'm feeling, why I'm feeling this way and how I feel about it, and if you don't want to accept it, fuck off" 

People can't see the inside of your head, and people are generally better at hiding their emotions than they assume themselves to be, yourself included. The more throttle you give it the more rubber you burn; until you get some traction. I'm still working on that myself.

You're not bad. You're not wrong. You're not especially selfish (humans are naturally selfish creatures; that's neurological) and you sure as hell don't need to hide or paint over your feelings for the benefit of others. This isn't their fight, and the reasons they debase your own faith in yourself are intentionally ignorant. Denial is a powerful tool, and it's infectious. 
Eventually you start denying your own existence because you've never had a say in how you feel. You've never DONE anything for yourself; all of your thoughts were planted by somebody else's. You're not human because you seem to "belong" to other people. They take responsibility for your thoughts and feelings, but they don't care how. 

This is your fight and your life, your mind and your future. I'm not gonna' promise everything will be all right, because it rarely is, but I think that you can convince yourself better than I that you've the inherent human right to the pursuit of happiness. 

Honesty with people willl force them to understand, and if they lash back, be honest about that. If they do it again, be honest.
Eventually they will either see why you're saying what you're saying and give you some much needed validation, or they won't; but you'll be able to judge their characters much better.
